correctness.rationale: For n>=5, common deletion descendants of size three are equivalent to intersection sum >=3. Distinct heavy codewords have distinct assigned coordinates, hence at most four. For two light vectors I>=2n-8, which prevents two at n>=6 and any light at n>=9. For n=5 compatible light pairs must each have exactly two 2-coordinates and these pairs are complementary, forbidding a third light. Four pure vectors plus two explicit light vectors at n=5, or one at n=6..8, meet the upper bounds. A standalone exact compatibility-clique search and explicit witness checker reproduce every finite boundary.

value.rationale: The motivating recent work explicitly treats retaining three symbols but leaves generally nonsharp bounds. The next nontrivial four-letter case has a complete infinite exact optimum profile with two distinct plateaux and a sharp transition at n=9. A natural heavy/light intersection obstruction accounts for each regime and gives constructive optima, making the result structurally useful rather than a standalone small-table enumeration.
